plan.headline: North Trail Cycles: all 11 entries ($56,770 in IEEPA tariffs paid) have a route to pursue. The first deadline is Nov 20, 2026.

steps.title: Withdraw your protest on one entry, then file it in CAPE
steps.detail: This entry has a protest filed only for the IEEPA refund. It appears eligible to be withdrawn and moved into CAPE (CBP's refund portal) while it is still within 80 days of liquidation (the date CBP finalized the duties). Ask your broker to do this before Nov 20, 2026.

steps.title: File this entry in CAPE before its cutoff
steps.detail: This entry appears eligible for CAPE now, but its 80-day window closes on Dec 10, 2026. Have your broker file it well before then.

steps.title: File these other entries in CAPE now
steps.detail: These appear eligible too, and no deadline came up. Filing soon is still wise. The first is covered by CAPE Phase 2, which is for entries flagged for reconciliation (a later duty adjustment filing).

steps.title: Check with your counsel on the court-case entries (Phase 3)
steps.detail: These were liquidated more than 80 days ago. Because you are a plaintiff in the Court of International Trade (CIT) case, they may qualify for CAPE Phase 3, open since Oct 6, 2026. Confirm with your counsel before anything is filed.

steps.title: Leave the open protest alone
steps.detail: This entry is past 80 days and already has a protest open, so it stays on the protest route. CAPE rejects entries with an open protest. Ask your broker for the protest's status.

steps.title: Ask your broker how CBP is treating two entries
steps.detail: One entry is of a type CAPE does not take today (such as AD/CVD, warehouse, or similar types). The other is linked to a drawback claim, which CAPE excludes. Your broker can say what route, if any, applies. Total for these two: $15,160.

plan.broker_email_subject: IEEPA tariff refunds: North Trail Cycles, action needed by Nov 20, 2026
plan.broker_email_body:
Hi,

I'm reviewing our IEEPA tariff refunds. Based on a rules check as of Oct 24, 2026, here is what I'd like your help with. Please confirm each item, since I'm relying on you for the final call.

1. Withdraw protest, then CAPE (by Nov 20, 2026): KT4-2209566-1 ($4,260). The protest was filed only for the IEEPA refund. Can you withdraw it and file the entry in CAPE before the 80-day window closes?

2. File in CAPE (by Dec 10, 2026): KT4-2209470-0 ($2,190).

3. File in CAPE, no deadline listed: KT4-2210384-7 ($1,960) and KT4-2209003-5 ($8,820). The second is flagged for reconciliation with no type 09 filed, so it looks like Phase 2.

4. Open protest: KT4-2208011-9 ($8,070). It is past 80 days with a protest already open. Can you update me on its status?

5. Entries I need your view on:
- KT4-2210027-4 ($11,660): it looks like a type CAPE doesn't take today (AD/CVD, warehouse, temporary importation, or reconciliation). How is CBP treating it?
- KT4-2209318-2 ($3,500): it is linked to a drawback claim, so it is excluded from CAPE. What are our options?

6. Court-case entries: KT4-2207145-6 ($9,440), KT4-2207698-3 ($3,180), KT4-2208260-1 ($2,430) and KT4-2208274-8 ($1,260). These may fall under CAPE Phase 3 because we are a CIT plaintiff. I'm confirming with our counsel and will let you know. Please tell me if you need anything from us.

Please let me know what you need from me and when.

Thank you,
North Trail Cycles Inc.

checker.summary: I checked all 11 entries against the 7501 pages and the activity report. The entry list is complete. The liquidation statuses and dates, the open-protest and IEEPA-only flags, and the reconciliation and drawback flags all match the documents. The Chapter 99 lines and amounts, and the stated IEEPA totals, also match the line detail and the report. The one problem is that KT4-2210027-4, a type 21 warehouse entry, is missing the warehouse type 21 flag.

warnings: Your documents say you are a plaintiff at the Court of International Trade (North Trail Cycles Inc. v. United States, Ct. No. 26-01417). Phase 3 routes assume that is true; confirm with your counsel. Phase 3 entries are not put in the CAPE file.
reader_notes: Every 7501 page is labeled 'synthetic sample - not a real filing'.
11 entries found. Each appears both on a 7501 page and in the broker's Account Activity Report, so each was merged into one record.
Page 11 of the 7501 file (KT4-2209566-1, entered 2025-10-27) is out of date order. It is filed after entries from November 2025 to February 2026.
Chapter 99 rows show a rate and duty but no entered value, so entered_value is null for those rows.
9903.01.24 appears at 20% on some entries and at 10% on others (KT4-2209470-0, KT4-2210384-7). Both are copied as printed.
KT4-2209003-5: the 7501 reconciliation note reads 'Y (NAFTA/value recon flagged)'. The broker report says 'Flagged for reconciliation; no type 09 filed yet.'
KT4-2210027-4 is a type 21 warehouse entry. The report says it is unliquidated with 'withdrawals ongoing'.
KT4-2208274-8: the report gives liquidation as 2026-04-26, which is a Sunday. Copied as stated; not checked against ACE.
Liquidation dates and statuses come only from the broker's activity report (run date 2026-10-21), not from CBP notices.
No document mentions surety payment or AD/CVD for any entry.
The broker letter says no CAPE declarations have been filed for any of these entries yet.
